newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi River remains closed near Baton Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi River remains closed near Baton Rouge.

text.p: A section of the Mississippi River north of Baton Rouge remained closed to barge traffic late Tuesday after a string of barges hit a bridge Monday, a Coast Guard official said.
"Anything that is north of Baton Rouge is not able to transit yet," said Commander Daniel Whiting, Chief of Port Operations, Coast Guard Marine Safety Office, New Orleans.
"We are working on getting (the river open) as rapidly as possible," he said. But Whiting said he expected traffic to remain closed into Wednesday.
"With a little bit of luck, we may work through it tomorrow (Wednesday)," he said. "People are working on this round-the-clock."
Whiting could not say how many barges were backed up as a result of the accident. "I don't have the count," he said.
"The Mississippi River is closed between river mile 233 (Baton Rouge) and river mile 235.5," he said.
Late Monday, a string of 25 barges hit a bridge in north Baton Rouge.
"At this point, we have one rock barge confirmed sunk and we have another four barges that were damaged and grounded but are being salvaged," Whiting said.
Whiting said one barge that was capsized and grounded was carrying a petroleum product that leaked into the waterway and cleanup efforts were under way.

No injuries were reported, but residents of 17 houses along that levee were evacuated. Whiting said the river would reopen when the navigation hazards have been removed and the chemical hazards no longer exist.
When the river reopens, he said, the Coast Guard will impose operational restrictions on the size of tows and horsepower required.
"Flood waters that are cresting between Memphis and Baton Rough have increased the current in the river and safe navigation requires extra precautions," Whiting said.
The cause of the accident was still being investigated, the Coast Guard said.
